stem: State Huygens' principle. Draw the shape of the wavefront for light (a) from a point source nearby, (b) from a distant star.
model_answer: *How much to write: statement and two small sketches · 3 minutes* **Huygens' principle:** every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets that spread out at the speed of the wave. The new wavefront at a later time is the forward envelope (common tangent) of these wavelets. **(a)** Point source nearby: spherical wavefronts, rays radially outward. **(b)** Distant star: plane wavefronts, rays parallel. :::tip Your answer must contain - "secondary wavelets" and "forward envelope" - both sketches with rays drawn perpendicular to the wavefronts ::: **Marks are lost for:** rays drawn along the wavefront; no envelope in the statement.

scheme.step: Every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets moving at the speed of the wave; the new wavefront is their forward envelope.
(a) Spherical wavefronts with radial rays; (b) plane wavefronts with parallel rays (diagrams).

hint: Each point on a wavefront sends out wavelets; the new wavefront is their forward envelope.

label: PYQ-style
stem: Give two differences between the interference pattern of a double slit and the diffraction pattern of a single slit.
model_answer:
*How much to write: two differences, one line each, best as a table · 2 minutes*

1. **Fringe width.** Interference: <u>all fringes equally wide</u>. Diffraction: the <mark>central maximum is twice as wide</mark> as the others.

2. **Brightness.** Interference: all bright fringes <u>equally intense</u>. Diffraction: intensity falls fast for higher orders.

(Also accepted: in interference the dark fringes are perfectly dark; in diffraction the minima are not; interference needs two coherent sources, diffraction comes from different parts of one wavefront.)

:::tip Your answer must contain
- two <u>paired</u> differences: each line says what happens in both patterns
:::

**Marks are lost for:** writing two points about one pattern only; vague words like "clearer" without saying width or intensity.

scheme.step: Interference: all fringes of equal width. Diffraction: central maximum twice as wide as the others.
Interference: all bright fringes equally intense (dark ones perfectly dark). Diffraction: intensity falls rapidly for higher orders (minima not perfectly dark).

hint: Compare the two patterns on fringe width and on how bright the successive bright fringes are.

stem: Light of wavelength 600 nm falls normally on a slit of width 0.2 mm. The pattern is seen on a screen 2 m away. Find (i) the angular position of the first minimum, (ii) the linear width of the central maximum, (iii) the new width if the slit width is halved.
model_answer:
*How much to write: about 6 lines · 5 minutes* **Given:** $\lambda=600$ nm, $a=0.2$ mm, $D=2$ m
**To find:** θ of the first minimum, width of the central maximum, width when $a$ is halved **(i)** $a\sin\theta=\lambda$, θ small: $$\theta\approx\frac{\lambda}{a}=\frac{600\times10^{-9}}{2\times10^{-4}}$$ $$\boxed{\theta=3\times10^{-3}\ \text{rad}}$$ **(ii)** $$w=\frac{2\lambda D}{a}=2\times3\times10^{-3}\times2$$ $$\boxed{w=1.2\times10^{-2}\ \text{m}=12\ \text{mm}}$$ **(iii)** $w\propto1/a$: $$\boxed{w=24\ \text{mm}}$$ A narrower slit spreads the light more. :::tip Your answer must contain - $a\sin\theta=\lambda$ for the first minimum - the factor 2 for the full central width - units rad and mm ::: **Marks are lost for:** width λD/a (forgetting the 2); 6 mm in (iii).
hint: First minimum: a sin θ = λ. Central maximum runs from −θ to +θ, so its width is 2λD/a.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) Use Huygens' principle to verify Snell's law of refraction for a plane wavefront going from a rarer to a denser medium. Draw the diagram. [3]
(b) In Young's experiment the fringe width is 3 mm with light of wavelength 600 nm. Find the fringe width with light of 400 nm, and the distance of the second dark fringe from the centre for 600 nm. [2]
model_answer:
*How much to write: about 12 lines with the Huygens diagram · 9 minutes* **(a)** A plane wavefront AB meets the surface AC at angle $i$. In the time $\tau$ that point B takes to reach C in medium 1, the secondary wavelet from A grows to radius $v_2\tau$ in medium 2. The tangent CE from C to this wavelet is the refracted wavefront. From the two right triangles: $$BC=v_1\tau=AC\sin i$$ $$AE=v_2\tau=AC\sin r$$ Dividing: $$\boxed{\frac{\sin i}{\sin r}=\frac{v_1}{v_2}=n_{21}}$$ This is Snell's law; since r < i, v₂ < v₁: light is slower in the denser medium. **(b) Given:** $\beta=3$ mm at $\lambda=600$ nm
**To find:** $\beta'$ at 400 nm; position of the 2nd dark fringe at 600 nm $$\beta=\frac{\lambda D}{d}\ \Rightarrow\ \beta\propto\lambda$$ $$\beta'=3\times\frac{400}{600}$$ $$\boxed{\beta'=2\ \text{mm}}$$ Dark fringes at $y=\left(n-\tfrac12\right)\beta$; for the 2nd, $n=2$: $$y=1.5\times3$$ $$\boxed{y=4.5\ \text{mm}}$$ :::tip Your answer must contain - a labelled diagram: AB, AC, wavelet radius $v_2\tau$, CE, angles $i$ and $r$ - $BC=v_1\tau$ and $AE=v_2\tau$ written as sines - the boxed ratio - (b) β ∝ λ, and $(n-\tfrac12)\beta$ for dark fringes ::: **Marks are lost for:** wavelet radius $v_1\tau$; mixing up which triangle gives sin i; taking 2β (6 mm) for the 2nd dark fringe.

scheme.step: (a) Diagram: incident wavefront AB, surface AC, wavelet of radius $v_2\tau$ centred at A, tangent CE (refracted wavefront), angles $i$, $r$.
Dividing: $\boxed{\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}=\dfrac{v_1}{v_2}=n_{21}}$, Snell's law (and $v_2<v_1$ in the denser medium).

hint: In the time the edge B of the wavefront reaches C, the wavelet from A grows to radius v₂τ in the denser medium.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) Using the idea of path difference, explain why bright and dark fringes are formed on the screen in Young's double-slit experiment. [2]
(b) The slits are 0.30 mm apart and the screen is 1.5 m away. Light of wavelength 600 nm is used. Find (i) the fringe width and (ii) the distance of the 4th bright fringe from the central maximum. [2]
(c) The whole set-up is now immersed in water (refractive index 4/3). Find the new fringe width. [1]
hint: Find the path difference first: d sin θ ≈ dy/D. The fringe width is λD/d, and the n-th bright fringe is n times that.
model_answer:
*How much to write: about 12 lines with one sketch: the path-difference idea, then the working in full with units · 10 minutes* **(a)** The two slits are coherent, so at a point P on the screen the waves arrive with path difference $\Delta x = S_2P-S_1P\approx d\sin\theta\approx\dfrac{dy}{D}$.
Where $\Delta x=n\lambda$ the waves reinforce and P is a bright fringe; where $\Delta x=(2n-1)\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$ they cancel and P is a dark fringe. **(b) Given:** $d=0.30$ mm $=3.0\times10^{-4}$ m, $D=1.5$ m, $\lambda=600$ nm $=6.0\times10^{-7}$ m
**To find:** $\beta$ and $y_4$ **(i) Formula:** $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$ $$\beta=\frac{6.0\times10^{-7}\times1.5}{3.0\times10^{-4}}=3.0\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}$$ $$\boxed{\beta=3.0\ \text{mm}}$$ (ii) The n-th bright fringe lies at $y_n=n\beta$, so the 4th one, counted from the centre, is at $$\boxed{y_4=4\times3.0\ \text{mm}=12\ \text{mm}}$$ **(c)** In water the wavelength becomes $\lambda'=\dfrac{\lambda}{\mu}=\dfrac{600}{4/3}=450$ nm. Only $\lambda$ changes; $D$ and $d$ stay the same. $$\begin{aligned}\beta'&=\frac{\lambda'D}{d}\\&=\frac{4.5\times10^{-7}\times1.5}{3.0\times10^{-4}}\\&=2.25\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}\end{aligned}$$ $$\boxed{\beta'=2.25\ \text{mm}}$$ — the fringes come closer together. :::tip Your answer must contain - the path difference as $dy/D$, with both conditions: nλ for bright and (2n−1)λ/2 for dark - β = λD/d with every value converted to metres first - $y_n=n\beta$ for the 4th bright fringe, counted from the central maximum - the new wavelength $\lambda/\mu$, with $D$ and $d$ unchanged ::: **Marks are lost for:** writing 3β or 4β + β for the 4th fringe; keeping λ unchanged in water; mixing mm and m in one line.

scheme.step: (a) Path difference $dy/D$ and the bright and dark conditions

stem: In a Young's double-slit set-up the slits are 0.3 mm apart and the screen is 1.5 m away. Light of wavelength 600 nm is used. Find (i) the fringe width, (ii) the distance of the fourth bright fringe from the central bright fringe, (iii) the new fringe width if the slit separation is doubled.
hint: Fringe width is $\beta=\lambda D/d$. Bright fringes lie at whole-number multiples of $\beta$ from the centre.
model_answer:
*How much to write: about 7 lines · 5 minutes* **Given:** $d=0.3$ mm, $D=1.5$ m, $\lambda=600$ nm
**To find:** $\beta$; the 4th bright fringe; $\beta$ when $d$ is doubled **(i)** Fringe width: $$\beta=\frac{\lambda D}{d}=\frac{600\times10^{-9}\times1.5}{0.3\times10^{-3}}$$ $$\boxed{\beta=3\ \text{mm}}$$ **(ii)** Bright fringes lie at $y_n=n\beta$ from the centre, so for $n=4$: $$\boxed{y_4=4\beta=12\ \text{mm}}$$ **(iii)** $\beta\propto 1/d$, so doubling $d$ halves the width: $$\boxed{\beta'=1.5\ \text{mm}}$$ A wider slit separation squeezes the fringes closer together. :::tip Your answer must contain - $\beta=\lambda D/d$ with every unit converted to metres - $y_n=n\beta$ for the bright fringe - $\beta\propto 1/d$ for the new value ::: **Marks are lost for:** forgetting to convert 0.3 mm to metres; $D/\lambda$ in place of $\lambda D/d$; giving 6 mm in part (iii).
